name: sdg01
title: SDG 1: No poverty (SDG Atlas of Bolivia 2026)
description: The SDG 1 (No poverty) index of the Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026 (SDSN Bolivia) and the 4 indicators behind it, for Bolivia's 343 municipalities and indigenous autonomies (GAIOC), at two points in time: near the 2012 census and near the 2024 census, stored as 2012 and 2024 so that their change can be studied.

sources.title: Andersen, L. E., & Argandoña, F. (2026). Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026: Brechas y tendencias del desarrollo sostenible en las Entidades Territoriales Autónomas, 2012–2024. La Paz: Universidad Privada Boliviana, SDSN Bolivia.
sources.geo:creator: Lykke E. Andersen and Fabiana Argandoña (SDSN Bolivia, Universidad Privada Boliviana)

geo:citation: GeoDevelopment Observatory of Bolivia (2026). SDG 1: No poverty, from the Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026 (343 municipalities, ~2012 and ~2024). https://github.com/quarcs-lab/geo4bolivia/blob/main/docs/datasets/sdg01.md
geo:notes: Both periods are stored at nominal years: 2012 for the Atlas's initial values (~2012) and 2024 for its final values (~2024). Each indicator's actual reference years differ (e.g. 2008 and 2023 for the health survey, three-year averages for volatile indicators) and are given in its description and in `geo:reference_years`.
Load one variable in both periods, e.g. `geo.load("sdg01", variables="index_sdg1")`, and its change with `df.pivot(index="geo_id", columns="year", values="index_sdg1")`.

The units are the 343 municipalities and indigenous autonomies (GAIOC) of 2025. Four of them were created after the 2012 census (TIOC-Raqaypampa, San Pedro de Macha, TIOC-Jatun Ayllu Yura and TIOC-Territorio Indígena Multiétnico); the Atlas gives them values in both periods.

The indicators are rates, shares, ratios or indices, so their aggregation rule is `none`. Population-weighted averages can use the census population of the `sdg` dataset: `geo.aggregate(df, to="department", rules={"index_sdg1": "weighted_mean:population"}, weights=geo.load("sdg", variables="population"))`.

fields.name: geo_id
fields.title: Municipality ID
fields.description: GDO-Bolivia municipality geo ID (BO-DD-PP-MM) of the 343-unit municipality map (SDSN Bolivia 2025: municipalities and indigenous autonomies), numbered as in GADM 4.1 plus four units created since; its boundary is in geo/boundaries/. It nests by prefix into the department (BO-DD) and province (BO-DD-PP) IDs; department and province numbers follow GADM order and differ from INE codes.

fields.name: year
fields.title: Period
fields.description: Period of the values in the row: 2012 holds the Atlas's initial values (near the 2012 census) and 2024 its final values (near the 2024 census). Each variable's actual reference years are given in its description and in geo:reference_years.

fields.name: mun_id
fields.title: INE municipality code
fields.description: Official municipality code of the National Statistics Institute (INE), DDPPMM (department, province, municipality) stored as an integer without the leading zero (e.g. 20101 = Nuestra Señora de La Paz), as in the Atlas. The Atlas's rows are linked to geo_id through this code.
fields.geo:source: Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026

fields.name: index_sdg1
fields.title: No poverty index (0-100)
fields.description: SDG 1 (No poverty) index of the Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026, on a 0-100 scale where 100 means the goal's targets are met and 0 the worst situation. Following the global SDG Index of SDSN, each of its 4 indicators is rescaled linearly to 0-100 between a worst and a best value (given in each indicator's description), with the direction set so that higher is always better and values beyond the bounds capped; the index is the simple mean of the available rescaled indicators. Components: Multidimensional poverty index (0-1); Energy poverty (% of dwellings); Unsatisfied basic needs (% of population); Access to the 3 basic services (% of households). Initial value (~2012) stored at 2012 and final value (~2024) at 2024; its components refer to different years around each census. Atlas: “Índice ODS1”.
fields.geo:source: Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026

fields.name: sdg1_2_mpi
fields.title: Multidimensional poverty index (0-1)
fields.description: Multidimensional poverty index MPI = A × H, where H is the share of households (in private dwellings) deprived in 3 or more of 9 indicators and A the average intensity (share of the 9 deprivations) among them. Multidimensional poverty follows Andersen & Branisa (2020): nine deprivations in three dimensions (resources: drinking water, electricity, sanitation; power and voice: an illiterate member aged 15+, a member aged 6+ without an identity card, no fixed or mobile phone; opportunities and choice: a birth in the last five years not attended by skilled personnel, a teenage pregnancy in the last five years, a member aged 6-19 not attending school). Source: own calculation of the Atlas from the INE Population and Housing Censuses of 2012 and 2024. Initial value 2012 (stored at 2012) and final value 2024 (stored at 2024). In the SDG 1 index it is rescaled linearly to 0-100 between 0.563 (worst, 0) and 0 (best, 100), lower is better, values beyond the bounds capped; the Atlas counts the target as met at 0.066 and major challenges from 0.23 on. Atlas indicator 01_02_02_01_mpi, “Índice de pobreza multidimensional” (Andersen & Argandoña 2026).
fields.geo:source: Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026

fields.name: sdg1_4_eep
fields.title: Energy poverty (% of dwellings)
fields.description: Percentage of dwellings whose annual residential electricity consumption is below the regional energy-poverty threshold: 252 kWh/year in the west (Chuquisaca, La Paz, Cochabamba, Oruro, Potosí, Tarija) and 516 kWh/year in the east (Santa Cruz, Beni, Pando); dwellings without a meter and meters with zero consumption also count as energy poor. Source: the residential electricity-meter database of the Ministry of Hydrocarbons and Energy for 2016 and 2024, compiled by Andersen et al. (2023). Initial value 2016 (stored at 2012) and final value 2024 (stored at 2024). In the SDG 1 index it is rescaled linearly to 0-100 between 100 (worst, 0) and 0 (best, 100), lower is better, values beyond the bounds capped; the Atlas counts the target as met at 15 and major challenges from 50 on. Atlas indicator 01_04_01_02_eep, “Tasa de pobreza energética (% de viviendas)” (Andersen & Argandoña 2026).
fields.geo:source: Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026

fields.name: sdg1_4_nbi
fields.title: Unsatisfied basic needs (% of population)
fields.description: Percentage of the population in private dwellings that is poor by unsatisfied basic needs (UBN), the INE measure of deprivation in housing (materials and space), basic services and energy, education (years completed, literacy, attendance) and health care. Source: INE tabulations of the INE Population and Housing Censuses of 2012 and 2024. Initial value 2012 (stored at 2012) and final value 2024 (stored at 2024). In the SDG 1 index it is rescaled linearly to 0-100 between 100 (worst, 0) and 0 (best, 100), lower is better, values beyond the bounds capped; the Atlas counts the target as met at 15 and major challenges from 50 on. Atlas indicator 01_04_01_03_nbi, “Porcentaje de la población con Necesidades Básicas Insatisfechas” (Andersen & Argandoña 2026).
fields.geo:source: Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026

fields.name: sdg1_4_ssb
fields.title: Access to the 3 basic services (% of households)
fields.description: Percentage of private dwellings with people present that have all three basic services: an improved water source, improved sanitation and electricity (INE criteria, which differ for urban and rural areas). Source: own calculation of the Atlas from the INE Population and Housing Censuses of 2012 and 2024. Initial value 2012 (stored at 2012) and final value 2024 (stored at 2024). In the SDG 1 index it is rescaled linearly to 0-100 between 0 (worst, 0) and 100 (best, 100), higher is better, values beyond the bounds capped; the Atlas counts the target as met at 85 and major challenges from 50 on. Atlas indicator 01_04_02_04_ssb, “Porcentaje de hogares con acceso a los 3 servicios básicos” (Andersen & Argandoña 2026).
